title: Felwood
body: Felwood was once the northern reach of Ashenvale, a serene forest tended by the night elves beneath Mount Hyjal. In the Third War the Burning Legion made it a weapon. To weaken the kaldorei before the demons marched on Hyjal, the dreadlord Tichondrius used the Skull of Gul'dan to poison the land, and nothing was spared: the trees blackened, the beasts went mad, ancients were twisted and the waters turned foul. Illidan Stormrage later took the skull and destroyed Tichondrius, yet the taint remained, and so did the demons. The Shadow Council plots with the Legion from Jaedenar, Jadefire satyrs defile the old elven ruins, and infernals still stalk the craters where they fell. The Deadwood furbolgs have been driven mad, while in the north the Timbermaw alone of their race stayed pure. From the Emerald Sanctuary, druids of the Emerald Circle labor to heal what they can. The Horde keeps Bloodvenom Post on the western cliffs, and the night elves hold Talonbranch Glade in the north.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Felwood (once part of northern Ashenvale; Archimonde had it corrupted before Hyjal; Tichondrius and the Skull of Gul'dan; Illidan took the skull and defeated Tichondrius; Shadow Council in Jaedenar; Bloodvenom Post only Horde post, Talonbranch the Alliance one)

title: Morlos'Aran
body: At the southern edge of Felwood, near the Ashenvale border, stand the ruins of Morlos'Aran. Before the Sundering it was a great night elf settlement, kin to Ameth'Aran in Darkshore and Ordil'Aran in Ashenvale, and its broken stones now serve only to recall a golden age lost long ago. The corruption has not spared it. Felpaw wolves, Angerclaw bears and Ironbeak owls roam among the ruins, and the great wolf Death Howl hunts these southern woods. Here the night elf druid Arathandris Silversky of the Emerald Circle keeps her post, seeking anyone willing to help her reclaim Felwood.

title: Emerald Sanctuary
body: Hidden among the trees of southern Felwood, the Emerald Sanctuary is the camp of the Emerald Circle, a largely independent branch of the Cenarion Circle sworn to undo the corruption of this land. Its druids are friendly to all who come in peace. The tauren Greta Mosshoof directs the war on the Shadow Council, Eridan Bluewind strikes at the Jadefire satyrs, and Taronn Redfeather searches for even a single pure source of water in the forest. Jessir Moonbow, come from Darnassus with her wolf Della, waits here for friends long overdue from Jaedenar. Nearby on the road stands Grazle, a Timbermaw furbolg seeking allies for his tribe.

parts.body: Word from Shatter Scar Vale ends Taronn's hopes. The craters there still hold the corrupt, fetid water that gathered in them years ago, and his search for even one pure source in Felwood has failed. Healing the land would have been far easier with it, so now he means to save what forest creatures he can and destroy those grown too corrupt to spare.

title: Deadwood Village
body: Southwest of the Emerald Sanctuary, toward the Ashenvale border, lies Deadwood Village, the chief camp of the Deadwood furbolgs. Like most of their race they fell to the fel, which poisons their minds and turns them against all others. Deadwood warriors, pathfinders and gardeners fill its huts, and the Timbermaw ask their allies to drive this camp back first. The village answers to Overlord Ror, a great befouled furbolg, and the savage Ragepaw prowls nearby. Ror is blamed for the loss of at least one hero: an orc warrior who roamed Felwood fighting the Shadow Council went after him at a druid's request, and neither was heard from again.

title: Ruins of Constellas
body: Northwest of the Emerald Sanctuary stand the Ruins of Constellas, once one of the many night elf settlements near Mount Hyjal. Its moonwell, long a symbol of renewal for the kaldorei, has been fouled with fel energy, and the Jadefire satyrs who hold the ruins use its waters to bring forth more of their kind. Their leader here is the cruel Xavathras, who spreads the sickness to every creature he can. Felsworn, shadowstalkers and rogues haunt the broken walls, cursed oozes seep among the stones, and the Forsaken of Bloodvenom Post have taken an interest in the well's water.

title: Jadefire Glen
body: In the south of Felwood, west of the Emerald Sanctuary, a wooded hollow called Jadefire Glen is one of the homes of the Jadefire satyrs, the tribe that has made the corruption of Felwood its feast. Satyrs and felsworn crowd the glade, and among them, seldom seen, walks Alshirr Banebreath. Even here a corrupted whipper root clings to life, sickly and slime coated, in desperate need of care if it is ever to be made whole.

title: Bloodvenom Post
body: Bloodvenom Post is the Horde's only foothold in Felwood, a small camp on the high cliffs above Darkshore, close by the poisoned Bloodvenom River. Braves stand guard, a wind rider master links it to the rest of Kalimdor, and merchants trade goods and weapons. Those who linger have their own purposes. The Forsaken Winna Hazzard experiments with corrupted moonwell water, Trull Failbane looks beyond Timbermaw to Winterspring and the night elf secrets its wildkin are said to guard, and the orc widow Dreka'Sur waits for vengeance on the furbolg who took her husband.

title: Bloodvenom Falls
body: Through the heart of Felwood runs the Bloodvenom River, its water thick with the forest's poison, and at Bloodvenom Falls it spills into fouled pools where tainted oozes breed. The largest of them, a hulking mass called the Ongar, lurks below the falls. The riverbanks belong to the Shadow Council: its warlocks, darkweavers and enforcers walk them openly, and the tunnels of their fortress run beneath.

title: Jaedenar
body: West of the road in central Felwood lies Jaedenar, raised on ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens and now named in worship of Kil'jaeden. It is the seat of the Shadow Council on Azeroth, the cult that claims credit for much of the suffering of the orcish people, and here it plots with the Burning Legion. Cultists, adepts and guardians patrol the ruins with their hounds, warlocks and darkweavers practice their arts, and legionnaires stand among them. At its center a moonwell still holds water, corrupt like all else here. Below lies Shadow Hold, the cult's fortress, warded by spells bound to burning braziers.

title: Shadow Hold
body: Beneath Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, the Shadow Council's chief fortress, and a single path winds down through it with no other way in. Four braziers of protection, called Pain, Malice, Hatred and Suffering, keep its depths hidden from scrying eyes. The cult keeps prisoners caged and torturers at hand. The warlock Ulathek has his own quarters here and boasts that he holds counsel with dreadlords, and in his chamber the dreadlord Lord Banehollow keeps court with his attendant Ur'dan. In the deepest halls waits one called Shadow Lord Fel'dan, attended by the succubi Moora and Salia.

title: Shrine of the Deceiver
body: Among the ruins of Jaedenar, one of the old druidic barrow dens has been given over to the Shadow Council and renamed the Shrine of the Deceiver, after Kil'jaeden, the lord of the Burning Legion whom the cult reveres. Where druids once slept, cultists, adepts and guardians keep its chambers with their hounds, and it is a dangerous place for the unprepared. The Emerald Circle sends would-be allies into these corrupted dens to thin the cult's ranks before trusting them with greater tasks.

title: Shatter Scar Vale
body: North of Bloodvenom Falls, east of the road, the land is pocked with craters where infernals were hurled down during the last great war. The craters still smolder and still hold the corrupt, fetid water that gathered in them years ago, and entropic beasts and horrors roam among them. The infernals themselves remain, brainless but destructive, and the mightiest of them is Immolatus. The vale has an unlikely resident too: the gnome warlock Niby the Almighty, who has made camp here with his imp near the burned-out remains of an infernal named Kroshius.

title: Jadefire Run
body: In the north of Felwood the Jadefire satyrs keep their second great encampment at Jadefire Run, ruled by the cruel Xavaric. Hellcallers and tricksters crowd the camp, feeding on the corruption of the forest's native creatures, and the beasts that roam its edges, Felpaw scavengers, Angerclaw maulers and Ironbeak hunters, carry that corruption plainly. Even the plants are sick: corrupted windblossoms, a night dragon and a whipper root struggle for life among the satyrs.

parts.body: Xavaric is more than one satyr chief among many. The Jadefire at the Ruins of Constellas were only part of a larger plan, cultivating the corrupted moonwell there so that its spoils could be delivered to him here.

Xavaric's simple wooden flute is far from simple. It was carved from an ancient protector, one of the treants that long guarded the night elves, and through fel magic the tortured spirit of that ancient remains bound within it, never released.

title: Irontree Woods
body: Irontree Woods spreads across northern Felwood, once a peaceful glade and now as corrupted as the rest of the forest. Crazed treants, the irontree stompers and wanderers, roam alongside warpwood elementals, toxic horrors and maddened grizzlies and owls. At the southern edge of the woods lie ruins where many corrupted treants once dwelt. Older presences are said to linger too. Vartrus, Stoma and Hastat, ancients who protected this forest and whose bodies were destroyed when the Legion marched upon Hyjal, are said to keep watch in spirit still, sharing their secrets only with those who prove worthy.

title: Irontree Cavern
body: A cavern beneath the Irontree Woods shelters warpwood elementals, moss flayers and shredders that the druids of the Emerald Circle believe are now beyond any hope of cleansing. Their sap, which the druids call blood amber, is studied by Arathandris Silversky and Maybess Riverbreeze in the hope of saving other life in Felwood, and killing these lost creatures is how both druids judge whether a stranger truly serves the Cenarion Circle. Deep in the cave lurks Dessecus, a powerful elemental.

title: Talonbranch Glade
body: Talonbranch Glade is a small night elf post in northern Felwood, south of Timbermaw Hold, built around a moonwell. It is the Alliance's only refuge in the corrupted forest. A hippogryph master links it to the other roosts of Kalimdor, and merchants offer weapons and supplies. Teachers keep the old disciplines alive here: Kaerbrus instructs hunters, Nalesette Wildbringer trains their pets, and the night elf druid Golhine the Hooded counsels that peace can be found anywhere, even within cold stone walls, by looking inward for balance. Golhine warns young druids that one day the Emerald Dream will call them to sleep for years and walk among the purest of forms.

title: Felpaw Village
body: In the far north of Felwood, just southwest of the gates of Timbermaw Hold, lies Felpaw Village, a camp of the Deadwood furbolgs. Den watchers, avengers and shamans guard it under Chieftain Bloodmaw, and corruption hangs heavy over its huts. Nafien, the Timbermaw guard at the nearby gate, grieves that his tribe must fight its own kin here. In the camp a cauldron bubbles with a rotting, repulsive sludge, and runners of the Winterfall tribe come down from Winterspring to carry shipments back to their village. The ritual totems its furbolgs carry give off a palpable despair.

title: Timbermaw Hold
body: Timbermaw Hold is the home of the Timbermaw furbolgs, cut into the mountains of northern Felwood, and its tunnels are the road from Felwood to Moonglade and Winterspring. While the forest outside rotted, the Timbermaw weathered the storm here, the only furbolg tribe to escape the corruption. They pay for it with suspicion. So many outsiders kill furbolgs on sight that the tribe trusts almost no one, and strangers who have not proven themselves are attacked within the hold. Nafien guards the Felwood gate and Salfa the Winterspring one. Inside, the gruff trader Gorn One Eye, Kernda, who studies the totems of the corrupted tribes, and Meilosh, who holds mooncloth sacred, deal with the few they trust.

Ownership: 1769 is Felwood's; Winterspring must not reuse quests 8481, 8484, 8485 or Gorn 11555. AreaTable 1769 belongs to Felwood (zones/felwood.txt). Kernda's study of totems rests on 8470 and 8471 (Deadwood and Winterfall ritual totems, 'through study and ritual').

title: Greta Mosshoof
body: Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid of the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary who leads the Circle's fight against the Shadow Council. She welcomes all who would protect this once mighty forest, but warns them not to be swayed by the power that soaks the land, for it will corrupt them as it corrupted Felwood. Her trust is earned in battle against the cult, and she explains why plainly: it weakens the foe, and it builds respect between allies. She prefers knowledge to haste, spying on Shadow Hold by scrying before any attack. She counts the shaman Islen Waterseer an old friend, and her prayers go to the Earthmother.
sources: quests 5157, 5158, 5165 texts (scrying, Islen an old friend, Earthmother)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. npc_text 3807 reread: classic. Her scrying plan and Islen are her character; the chain's outcomes are in 36128 parts. Earlier: Verifier: verified (tauren female by display 10253). Has gossip menu 3074. Her chain is told in the story entry; this entry keeps to her character.

title: Eridan Bluewind
body: Eridan Bluewind is a night elf druid of the Emerald Circle who works from the Emerald Sanctuary. She notes the bitter truth that Felwood is named for the very thing that corrupted it, yet she still believes the corruption can one day be erased. Her chief enemies are the Jadefire satyrs, who spread their disease to every creature they meet, and she means to defend a land that was once her people's. Seekers of Un'Goro Crater's mysteries find their way to her as well.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Eridan_Bluewind (night elf druid, female, Emerald Sanctuary before 4.0.3a)
notes: Converted: her sense of something larger than the satyrs (4421 reward) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 4421; feeling the bound ancient (939 reward, 4441 description) to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 939 and QUEST_ACCEPT 4441; breaking the bond (4442) to part 3 on QUEST_DONE 4442. Parts are Alliance only (quests races 1101); the entry stays faction 0 (TALK 9116, template 35). Opening adds 'a land that was once her people's' from the 4421 description. npc_text 3874 and creature_text 9116 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Gossip menu 3142. The Linken/Un'Goro quests belong to Un'Goro and are not triggers.

parts.body: Even with Xavathras slain, Eridan is not at ease. She senses something much larger than the satyrs at work in Felwood, and warns that ridding the forest of one cruel satyr is only the first step in a long labor of repair.

She is sensitive to more than satyrs. Holding the flute taken from Xavaric is almost unbearable to her, for in it she feels the suffering of ancient ones: a protector's spirit, bound and tortured by fel magic and never released.

With blessed water from the Temple of the Moon and a prayer that Elune guide her hands and heart, Eridan banishes the evil aura from the flute and breaks the link between it and the ancient spirit bound within.

title: Lord Banehollow
body: Lord Banehollow is a dreadlord of the Burning Legion, one of the nathrezim, and he keeps a chamber of his own within Shadow Hold, the Shadow Council's fortress beneath Jaedenar. His attendant Ur'dan waits close at hand, and the warlocks, darkweavers and legionnaires of the Hold keep the halls around him. To any mortal who reaches his chamber uninvited he is a deadly foe, a demon lord who meets intrusion with his dark magic rather than with words.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lord_Banehollow (dreadlord, leader of Jaedenar, rival Hel'nurath, Ulathek a spy, Ur'dan attendant)
quests 7623 (Shadowy Potions, reward text on patience), 7624 (Ulathek plots with Hel'nurath on Xoroth, heart), 7625 (Xoroth domain of Hel'nurath, stardust from Ur'dan at a price)
gameobject 175724 Sargeras and the Betrayal, page_text 1776 (the Nathrezim, also known as dreadlords); quest 13251 description (dreadlords known racially as the Nathrezim)
notes: Check: 'nathrezim' kept: the in-game book Sargeras and the Betrayal (page_text 1776) and quest 13251 name the dreadlords' race in 3.3.5 text. Guards confirmed in both setups: Ur'dan 15 yards away, Jaedenar Legionnaires 58 to 75, Warlocks about 100, Darkweavers about 120 (mod-individual-progression changes only his and their SmartAI, no spawns); 'dark magic' holds either way (Shadow Shock and Curse of Thorns in both scripts). Converted for group kill credit: the opening (KILL 9516, TALK 9516) now tells only what a bystander at the fight sees: a dreadlord in his chamber in Shadow Hold with Ur'dan beside him, hostile to all (template 1434); the nearby guards named are the spawns within 150 yards (Jaedenar Legionnaire, Warlock, Darkweaver). His spells are not named, since mod-individual-progression replaces his SmartAI in zone_felwood.sql. The warlock chain moved to parts: his rank, patience and Ulathek's treachery to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 7623, turned in to him in Shadow Hold, and QUEST_ACCEPT 7624, offered by RewardNextQuest); the heart and the stardust to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 7624, QUEST_ACCEPT 7625). 7623-7625 are warlock-only (QuestSortID -61) and start or end with Banehollow; QUEST_ACCEPT 7623 and QUEST_DONE 7625 (Gorzeeki, Burning Steppes) are not used. Earlier: Verifier: 'burning world' replaced by 7625's own words (Hel'nurath's domain, famed dreadsteeds); 'guards him' for Ur'dan unsupported, dropped. Faction 0 confirmed: template 1434 (faction 869) has hostile mask 1 (all players), no friend mask, so both factions can kill him; TALK works only for warlocks of either side via the Shadowy Potions (7623 races 595 span both factions). Faction 1434 is hostile to all players, so the TALK trigger works only for warlocks with the Shadowy Potions; KILL keeps the entry open to everyone (rank 1 elite). Faction 0. Burning Steppes' Altar of Storms tells Mor'zul's dreadsteed rite; 7623-7625 are not used as triggers. 'burning world' of Xoroth matches Burning Steppes' 'burning Plains of Xoroth'.

parts.body: Those who come cloaked in the Shadow Council's own brand of evil may speak with him, for he is the dreadlord of Jaedenar, the cult's seat. His patience, he says, spans the millennia, yet he grants a mortal no more than an instant of it. Favor is earned in blood: his groveling servant Ulathek is a spy for his rival, Lord Hel'nurath of Xoroth, who means to usurp his power, and Banehollow wants the traitor's heart.

The heart pleases him. After a week of rotting, he says, it will make a succulent treat, and perhaps he will send for Ulathek's head to set before him as he eats. His patience grows, marginally. To one who would open a portal to Xoroth, Hel'nurath's domain and home of the famed dreadsteeds, he allows a store of Xorothian stardust from Ur'dan, if the price is paid.

title: Niby the Almighty
body: Niby the Almighty is a gnome warlock camped in Shatter Scar Vale with his imp Impsy, and he commands every visitor to bow in his presence, certain they can feel the power he holds over them. His ambitions run to infernals. Nearby lie the burned out remains of one called Kroshius, and to a fellow warlock who rekindles that corpse, destroys it and brings back the infernal core from its burning remains, Niby will teach the secret of summoning an infernal servant. Impsy, for his part, privately considers his master daft.
sources: creature_text 14469 (bow down, kicked out of Stormwind, infernal destroyer, chicken, death by chicken)
quests 7601, 7602, 7603 (infernal core of Kroshius, teach summoning an infernal servant)
notes: Converted: the chicken conjuration moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 7603 (smart_scripts 1446900 runs on that turn-in; 7603 is warlock only, races 0, so both factions' warlocks earn it). The opening keeps his gossip (npc_text 7001), the 7601 offer and Impsy's view of him (7602 completion text). Creature and npc texts reread: classic. Check: the Stormwind grudge ('cone heads', 'kick me out') dropped from part 1: it is creature_text 14469 group 3, which no script says (1446900 says Niby 0, 1, 2 and Impsy 0, 1); the vengeance and 'Death to Stormwind' of group 2 stay. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Both NPCs friendly (faction 35) and talkable; the warlock quests are class-limited so no quest triggers. El Pollo Grande's later rampage to Gadgetzan (wiki) left out.

parts.body: Once the core is his, Niby orders everyone to stand well back, for his greatest conjuration needs a wide berth. He bids the world bow down before his infernal destroyer, and from the sky falls a chicken. Impsy rolls on the floor laughing and tells his master he is an idiot. Niby silences his servant, undaunted: vengeance will be his, and Stormwind will meet death by chicken.
sources: smart_scripts 1446900 (run on 7603 rewarded: Niby groups 0, 1, 2 and Impsy groups 0, 1)

title: Arko'narin
body: Arko'narin is a night elf held captive by the Shadow Council, locked in a cage within Shadow Hold beneath Jaedenar. Cold and hungry, she begs anyone who comes near to help her escape, certain that one of her captors carries the key. She did not come alone. Her friend Trey was taken with her, and she fears he is already dead, unable to bear the thought of what the cultists may have done to him. She still believes there is time to save herself, though she is sure that before long they will sacrifice her to whatever demons they worship.
sources: quest 5203 description and reward (Lightforge, superiors, Darnassus, no time for the druids)
quest 5204 completion text (Knight of the Silver Hand)
notes: Check: gossip 3129 shows 3865 by default, 4113 once 5202 is rewarded (condition 14/3129/4113) and 4114 once 5203 is rewarded; the cage opens only on ACCEPT 5203 (smart_scripts 11016 sets gameobject 176306), so part 1 now opens 'With the key in her hands' rather than 'Freed from the cage'. Converted: the opening is now her plea from the cage (npc_text 3865, 5202 completion text), seen before she is freed; her account of the capture (npc_text 4113, shown once the key is used) and Lightforge moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 5202 and QUEST_ACCEPT 5203; the escape, Trey's spirit and Darnassus to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 5203. 'Human' dropped for Trey: only his displays show it. npc_text 3865, 4113 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: Trey is a human male (remains 11020 and spirit 11141 use human male displays 10425, 10641; wiki). Arko'narin still not called a warden. Faction 0 confirmed: template 250 friendly to all players. Captured Arko'narin 11016 has gossip 3129. The escape is told in the story entry; this keeps to her and her friendship. 'warden' (wiki) not used.

parts.body: With the key in her hands, she tells her story. She and her longtime friend Trey Lightforge came to Jaedenar to investigate the Shadow Council, but the cult caught them unprepared, took all their equipment and dragged Trey deeper into the Hold. She can still hear his screams from below, inhuman, and swears the cultists will pay. She will not leave without his sword, Lightforge, and she must warn her superiors.

Arko'narin wins her way out, though the escape costs her the sight of Trey's tormented spirit turned against her. She carries Lightforge on to Darnassus, too urgent even to stop for the druids' healing. She does not show it, but her friend Jessir Moonbow knows that losing one of her closest friends, a Knight of the Silver Hand, is tearing her up inside.

title: Arei
body: Arei is the spirit of one of Felwood's ancient protectors, bound to the land's suffering even after death. Arei remembers a peaceful and serene forest before the Legion came with its infernals, destruction and chaos, and the Skull of Gul'dan, which ensured that nothing was spared: all fell to the corruption. Trapped by it still, the spirit cannot rest, and asks only to be led through the cursed forest toward home, where it may finally be at peace. Once free, Arei bids its guide seek out the druid Kayneth Stillwind in Forest Song, in eastern Ashenvale.
sources: quest 4261 description, log and reward (Kayneth: every kind deed helps)
ashenvale.json Kayneth notes (4261 left to Felwood)
notes: Converted: the escort and Arei's release (creature_text 9598 lines during the escort, 4261 reward text) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 4261; the opening is the 4261 description and its gossip (npc_text 2726). creature_text 9598 and npc_text 2726, 2809 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: faction 1 confirmed: Arei 9598 has no standing spawn (summoned only by event 3839), 939/4441/4442/4261 are AllowableRaces 1101, and template 79 is hostile to the Horde. Faction 1: 4261 AllowableRaces 1101 and Arei is summoned only by the Alliance flute chain (4442). Arei is not a standing spawn. Arei Transformed 9599 not used. Kayneth's TALK trigger stays with Ashenvale.

parts.body: The way out is hard. Maddened creatures fall upon the spirit, and Arei grieves that it must fight its own kind, urging that the fel touched beasts be put out of their misery. As Ashenvale draws near, Arei's form changes: the true strength of its spirit returns and the cursed grasp of the forest leaves it, and at last it is at peace. Kayneth, hearing of it, holds that Felwood may one day be reclaimed, for every kind deed helps.

title: Grazle
body: Grazle is a Timbermaw furbolg who stands on the road near the Emerald Sanctuary, far from his tribe's hold, seeking friends among outsiders. He calls the Timbermaw the last of the furbolg race to remain uncorrupted, and it pains him that few believe such a thing possible. Most strangers kill furbolgs on sight, and in anger his brethren now attack anyone who comes near. Grazle still hopes that peace can be made with those who show by their deeds that they come as allies. To any who fight the corrupted Deadwood, he is a patient friend, and he makes sure their deeds are known among his kind.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. npc_text 4393 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Gossip 3622. His quests 8460 and 8466 are the story's.

title: Gorn One Eye
body: Gorn One Eye keeps a trader's stall deep within Timbermaw Hold, dealing with the few outsiders his tribe has come to trust. He is warier than most of his kin. To a stranger who has won over only a handful of the Timbermaw he has little to say: he sees them, they may be on their way, and it will take more than the trust of a few to prove anything to him. Yet in time it is Gorn who brings the tribe's gravest task to those who have earned its trust.
sources: quest 8481 description and reward (summon the demon at High Chief Winterfall's cave, Essence of Xandivious, chance at survival)
quests 8484, 8485 (offering of peace to Magni and Thrall, who had tried to make contact)
notes: Converted: the opening is his gossip (npc_text 4399) and his role as the giver of 8481; the demon behind the Winterfall moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8481), Xandivious's fall to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 8481), the offering of peace to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8484 or 8485, offered by Gorn) and its reception to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 8484 at Magni, 8485 at Thrall). Parts 3 and 4 name no leader, since each faction's quest names only its own. Check: 'the Timbermaw do not forget their allies' (Nafien's 8461 completion text) dropped from the opening, since a visitor who reaches Gorn through Winterspring need not have heard it. Ownership unchanged: 8481, 8484, 8485 and Gorn 11555 are Felwood's. npc_text 4399 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: Xandivious is summoned at the cave mouth (8481), not said to rule from the cave; reworded. Faction 0 confirmed (8481 races 0; template 414 Timbermaw rep, open to both). Winterspring must not reuse 8481, 8484, 8485 or Gorn 11555. 8481 starts and ends with Gorn in Timbermaw Hold (QuestSortID 1769) though the fight is in Winterspring; Winterspring should not reuse 8481/8484/8485 or 11555. Gorn's gossip needs Timbermaw reputation; both factions can earn it. 'partially sighted' from the wiki not used.

parts.body: That task is the root of all evil for the Winterfall. Thanks to the tribe's friends, the Timbermaw have found a way to draw out the demon that dominates their corrupted kin: a torch planted at the mouth of High Chief Winterfall's cave will force it to show itself, and only the essence of the fallen demon can begin the Winterfall's long healing, and the salvation of Timbermaw Hold.

When the essence of the demon Xandivious is brought to him, Gorn's gruffness gives way. The safety of Timbermaw Hold is assured for years to come, he declares, and its slayer is a hero among the furbolgs. The healing will be slow and the conflict will go on, but the Winterfall have something they never had before: a chance at survival.

Gorn then looks beyond his own kind. Deeds such as these go beyond the tale of a simple hero, he says, and if the hero speaks for a people, the Timbermaw would make peace with them. He sends an offering of peace to the leader of the hero's people, who in times past tried to make contact with his tribe.

The offering is received as a most fortuitous turn of events. A lasting peace with the Timbermaw would give the hero's people a real advantage in Kalimdor, and word of it goes out at once to the other leaders, with more diplomats to follow.

title: Dreka'Sur
body: Dreka'Sur is an orc of Bloodvenom Post whose husband traveled Felwood for the honor of their clan, battling the Shadow Council and the forest's other abominations. He cheated death many times. His last letter told her that a druid had asked his help against a great befouled furbolg called Overlord Ror, and after that neither warrior nor druid was heard from again. Left a widow and unable to rest, Dreka'Sur wants Ror's clawed hand, caring nothing whether the beast is corrupt or merely savage from living in so dismal a forest, so long as it pays for its crimes against her family.
sources: quest 6162 description, completion and reward text
notes: Converted: the claw's delivery and her comfort (6162 reward text) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 6162; the opening keeps the 6162 description and completion text. Earlier: Verifier: faction 2 confirmed: template 1074 friendly to Horde, hostile to Alliance; 6162 races 690. Female orc by display 8890. Faction 2: template 1074 (enemy group Alliance), 6162 AllowableRaces 690. No gossip menu; quest dialog opens.

parts.body: When Ror's claw is brought to her, Dreka'Sur counts it an honor kept. Her husband died in battle, she says, and he would have been proud of that, but she could not rest until the creature that left her to live her life alone had paid for what it had done.

title: Winna Hazzard
body: Winna Hazzard is a Forsaken at Bloodvenom Post who admits that some call her exceptionally cruel, though she insists she only wants the Horde to gain every advantage over the Alliance, in any way possible. Her newest interest is the corrupted moonwell at the Ruins of Constellas, south of the post, once a symbol of renewal for the night elves and now a font that brings forth more satyrs. She has an idea for its water, and wants a sample brought to her for the sake of her little feline friend, the kitten that keeps her company.
sources: creature_text 9996 (pours the water on the cat, perfect)
notes: Converted: the kitten's growth and the trip to the well (4506 description) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 4505 and QUEST_ACCEPT 4506; the corrupted saber and her plans (4506 reward) to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 4506. 'Laughing' dropped: creature_text 9996 has no script that says it. Check: the transformation is traced: item 12565 casts 15647 Summon Common Kitten (9937) at the moonwell (spell focus 644); its actionlist 993700 says 'jumps into the moonwell, and goes underwater', updates its template to Corrupted Saber 10042, which emotes 'follows $n obediently' and follows the player back, where gossip 55002 gives the 4506 credit. Earlier: Verifier: faction 2 confirmed: template 68 friendly to Horde, hostile to Alliance; 4505 races 690. Female Forsaken by display 9343. Faction 2: template 68 (Undercity, enemy group Alliance), 4505 AllowableRaces 690. Cataclysm slime experiments left out. 6605 (A Strange One) ends with her but starts in Winterspring; not used.

parts.body: The sample works as she hoped. A little of the water made her kitten double in size and grow stronger, somehow, and Winna wants the cat carried to the moonwell itself and released there, promising with a chuckle that the results will please. Such cats, she thinks, may prove useful.

What comes back from the moonwell is no kitten but a corrupted saber, following its keeper obediently. Winna is delighted: the Forsaken, she says, will resort to any means necessary to crush the Alliance, and the corrupted water will surely prove useful in their future efforts.
sources: spell 15647, smart_scripts 9937 and actionlist 993700 (kitten turned into 10042 at the moonwell)

title: The Shadow Council in Jaedenar
body: Greta Mosshoof of the Emerald Circle will not trust anyone against the Shadow Council until they have proven themselves its enemy, for the cult is responsible for many evils in Felwood and far beyond it. Its seat is Jaedenar, along a path to the west, where it plots with the Burning Legion. So her would-be allies first descend into one of the corrupted barrow dens there to slay its hounds, guards, adepts and cultists. She knows that shedding blood as proof of honor disgusts some, but it serves two ends: it weakens the foe, and it builds a respect between allies that will make them stronger in the times to come.
sources: quests 5155, 5157, 5158, 5159, 5165, 5242 descriptions, completion and reward texts
notes: Converted: the opening is the 5155 premise and completion text; parts follow the chain: 1 the braziers and the canteen (QUEST_DONE 5155, QUEST_ACCEPT 5157, RewardNextQuest), 2 Islen (QUEST_DONE 5157, QUEST_ACCEPT 5158, both at Greta), 3 the spirits' blessing and warning (QUEST_DONE 5159 at Greta, QUEST_ACCEPT 5165), 4 the braziers doused (QUEST_DONE 5165), 5 Fel'dan named (QUEST_ACCEPT 5242), 6 his fall (QUEST_DONE 5242). QUEST_DONE 5158 and QUEST_ACCEPT 5159 (at Islen in the Barrens) are not used; all six quests are QuestSortID 361 and races 0. Earlier: Verifier: Islen's step condensed to one clause; barrens.json Tidus Stair gives her side, no trigger shared (5158/5159 unused). Faction 0 confirmed (all quests races 0, Greta template 35). 5155 is the only entry point (5157 requires it). The Barrens' Tidus Stair entry mentions the water being carried to Islen; no shared triggers (5158/5159 unused). Taronn's 5156 is told in Shatter Scar Vale.

parts.body: With the cult's numbers thinned, Greta reveals her plan. Shadow Hold, the fortress deep within Jaedenar, is guarded by protective spells bound to braziers, and while they burn her scrying cannot reach inside to learn who leads the Council. Purified water could douse them, so a canteen is carried to the Moon Well at the center of Jaedenar and filled with its corrupt water.

Purifying it will take travel. Greta sends the water to the Barrens, to a small camp on the shore south of Ratchet, where her old friend, the shaman Islen Waterseer, keeps a strong bond with the spirits of water. A cause so noble, Greta trusts, should persuade both Islen and the spirits to help.

The spirits judge the cause just, and Islen sends the purified water back with her regards and a warning: the Shadow Council is not a force to be trifled with, and Greta is tackling something greater than many know. Greta takes heart from the blessing, and the water is carried into Shadow Hold to douse the four braziers of protection.

As the last brazier's flame dies, Greta's spells pierce the Hold, and before the Council's warlocks can restore their wards she learns enough, she hopes, to strike. Going into a dragon's lair without knowledge is a fool's errand, she says, and the Shadow Council is far worse than any dragon.

What she learned points to one man. There is no other way into Shadow Hold than the straight path down, and at its bottom waits Shadow Lord Fel'dan, the mortal in power below, the head of the serpent and the one making pacts with the Legion. He and his two succubus servants must die.

Fel'dan falls with his succubi, Moora and Salia, and his head is carried back to the Emerald Sanctuary. Greta praises the Earthmother: with such a blow to its hierarchy the Council will be hard pressed to regain its old power, and without Fel'dan she hopes it will lose focus and turn to infighting, the moment to strike its demons hardest.

title: The Prisoner of Shadow Hold
body: Jessir Moonbow came from Darnassus to meet two friends at the Emerald Circle's camp near the Ashenvale border, but they are days late. They had gone into Jaedenar to learn whether the Shadow Council, which claims credit for much of the orcish race's suffering, is regaining its power. Among the cult's servants, meanwhile, some carry a strange key, small and red and made of some kind of bone, heavy in the hand yet very fragile. Why a member of the Shadow Council would carry such a thing is a mystery, and somewhere in Jaedenar there must be something it unlocks.
sources: smart_scripts 11016 (escort, summons Jaedenar Legionnaires 9862 and Spirit of Trey Lightforge 11141)
item 13140 Blood Red Key drops from Jaedenar warlocks, darkweavers, enforcers, legionnaires, Ulathek and Ur'dan
gameobject 176225 Arko'niran's Chest; Rakaiah 9518 near the Remains of Trey Lightforge 11020
notes: Check: part 1 no longer says she is freed on DONE 5202 (the cage opens on ACCEPT 5203). Converted: the opening is Jessir's premise (npc_text 3864) and the key (5202 description); parts: 1 the cage and Lightforge (QUEST_DONE 5202, QUEST_ACCEPT 5203), 2 the escape, Trey's spirit and Jessir's request (QUEST_DONE 5203, QUEST_ACCEPT 5204, RewardNextQuest), 3 Rakaiah and the remains (QUEST_DONE 5204 at the Remains of Trey Lightforge, QUEST_ACCEPT 5385, item-started), 4 the remains returned (QUEST_DONE 5385). KILL 9518 not used. npc_text 3864, 3865, 4113 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: the cage stands near the top of Shadow Hold (Arko'narin at z 319; 5203 speaks of the path to the top), so 'deep in' made 'within'. Faction 0 confirmed (5202 races 0, Arko'narin template 250 and Jessir 35 friendly to all). 5202 (item-started) is the only entry point. Jessir is not given a person entry; her TALK 11019 is left unused.

parts.body: The key fits a cage within Shadow Hold, and in it is the night elf Arko'narin, one of Jessir's missing friends. Even once the cage is open she will not simply flee: first she must recover the sword Lightforge, which belonged to her companion Trey, along with her own gear, and escape the Hold to warn her superiors of what is happening there.

The escape is hard won. Arko'narin finds her gear among candles laid out for some dark ritual and fights her way out past the cult's legionnaires, and then Trey himself appears, his tormented spirit turned against her. She hurries on to Darnassus with Lightforge, and Jessir, knowing how the loss of this Knight of the Silver Hand will haunt her friend, asks for his torturer, the succubus Rakaiah, to be slain and his remains found.

Rakaiah is slain, and near her lie the remains of Trey Lightforge, beyond doubt the Knight of the Silver Hand who came into Jaedenar with Arko'narin. They are gathered with care, and there is comfort in knowing that at least his spirit has been released from the pain forced upon it.

Carried back to Jessir on the border of Felwood and Ashenvale, the remains can at last be given proper respect. Jessir gives thanks to Elune, certain that Arko'narin will be glad her rescuer not only saved her but also slew the creature who tortured one of her best friends.

title: The Jadefire Satyrs
body: Few seek adventure in Felwood, where the corruption is widespread and indiscriminate. Eridan Bluewind of the Emerald Circle means to heal the land, but some wish it to fester, and chief among them are the Jadefire satyrs at the Ruins of Constellas, northwest of the Sanctuary. Led by a particularly cruel satyr named Xavathras, with felsworn, shadowstalkers and rogues at his command, they spread their disease to every creature they meet. Eridan means to defend a land that was once her people's, and the first blow must fall on Xavathras and his minions.
notes: Converted: the opening is the 4421 premise; Xavathras's fall and the reveal of Xavaric and the moonwell moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 4421, QUEST_ACCEPT 4906); Xavaric's fall to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4906). 'Betrayers' still left out (no Jadefire Betrayer 7108 spawn). Earlier: Verifier: betrayers dropped (Jadefire Betrayer 7108 has no spawn). Faction 1: 4421 and 4906 AllowableRaces 1101. 4906 requires 4421.

parts.body: Xavathras's death is only the first step in a long process of repair, and Eridan senses something larger than the satyrs at work. Part of the truth soon follows: Xavathras and his minions served a larger plan, cultivating the corrupted moonwell at Constellas to provide its spoils to Xavaric, whose camp lies to the north, where hellcallers and tricksters feed upon the corruption of the forest's native creatures.

In the north Xavaric falls among his hellcallers and tricksters, and his camp's torment of Felwood's creatures is ended. Eridan gives thanks and asks that Elune protect and guide her champion on the path ahead, knowing that the long labor of healing the forest has only begun.

title: The Flute of Xavaric
body: Among the spoils of Xavaric, master of the Jadefire satyrs in northern Felwood, is a simple wooden flute. Its knotted wood feels solid, yet the spirals and patterns on its surface seem to spin and move as it is turned in the hand, and whoever holds it is seized by a sudden dread. Perhaps the mind is only playing tricks. Other satyrs may carry clues to what it is, and the felbind they bear seems worth gathering, so the flute is taken south to the druid Eridan Bluewind of the Emerald Sanctuary.
notes: Check: Eridan's call to banish the evil aura (creature_text 9116, said on ACCEPT 4442) moved out of part 2, which DONE 4441 alone also unlocks, into part 3 (DONE 4442). Converted: the opening is the 939 premise (item-started from Xavaric's flute); Eridan's reading of the flute moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 939, QUEST_ACCEPT 4441, RewardNextQuest), the purification to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4441, QUEST_ACCEPT 4442), the broken link and the ruins to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 4442), Arei's summoning to part 4 (QUEST_ACCEPT 4261, whose giver Arei appears only when the flute is played). The escort itself is told in 36123. creature_text 9116 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Faction 1: 939 AllowableRaces 1101; item 11668 starts it. The Arei escort (4261) is told in Arei's person entry.

parts.body: Eridan can hardly bear to hold it. She senses the suffering of ancient ones: the flute was carved from an ancient protector, one of the treants that long guarded the night elves, and through fel magic the satyrs have bound its spirit to suffer without release. The felbind is surely part of it. To purify the flute she needs blessed water from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

The blessed water is brought from Darnassus, and Eridan prays that it will release the ancient's spirit and let it rest. With the water of Elune she begins the purification, asking that Elune guide her hands and heart.

As she prays, Eridan feels the presence of evil leaving the flute, and the link between flute and spirit is broken. She believes the flute may now summon the spirits of ancients if played in a sacred place, perhaps the ruins in the southern part of Irontree Woods, where many corrupted treants once lived and where they may linger still, even in spirit form.

Played among those ruins, the flute brings forth Arei, the spirit of an ancient protector still trapped by Felwood's corruption, who begs to be led out of the cursed forest so that it may finally rest.

title: Cleansing Felwood
body: Two druids of the Emerald Circle, the night elf Arathandris Silversky southeast of the Emerald Sanctuary and the tauren Maybess Riverbreeze to its west, know how to cleanse the forest's sick plants, but they guard that knowledge closely, for in the wrong hands it would spell disaster for all of Felwood. Plants give life to the forest, and even they suffer the taint. Trust must be won first in the Irontree Cavern to the north, where warpwood elementals lost beyond any hope of cleansing are slain for the sap called blood amber, which the druids study in the hope of saving other life.
sources: quest 4103 completion and reward (beacon, soul shards, salve)
quests 996, 2523, 4117, 4119 texts (corrupted windblossom, songflower, whipper root, night dragon)

parts.body: With the blood amber delivered, trust is given. It may seem odd that killing the elementals proved anything, the druid admits, but saving countless lives must justify the means. Then the craft is shared. A Cenarion beacon lets its bearer see the corruption the naked eye misses, and the corrupted soul shards that tainted beasts leave behind, and from such shards the druids grind the reagent for Cenarion plant salve.

Spread on one of Felwood's sick plants, whether songflower, windblossom, night dragon or slime coated whipper root, the Cenarion plant salve works at once. The plant sheds its corrupted form and blossoms vibrant and healthy again, one small patch of the old forest given back its life.
sources: gameobject_queststarter: 29 Corrupted Songflower, Windblossom, Whipper Root and Night Dragon quests, QuestSortID 361, QuestType 0

title: Timbermaw Ally
body: Grazle of the Timbermaw knows that outsiders kill furbolgs without asking whether they are friend or foe, so his tribe, the only one of its race to escape the corruption, trusts very few. To earn a place among its allies one must drive back the corrupted Deadwood, starting with the warriors, pathfinders and gardeners of the village southwest of the Sanctuary. At the far end of the road, Nafien, who guards the gate of Timbermaw Hold, asks the same of the Deadwood camp to his southwest, though he begs to be spared the details: the Deadwood are not evil by nature, only poisoned by the fel, and it grieves him to fight his own brethren.
sources: quest 8465 reward (Winterfall under the same corruptive sway)
notes: Check: part 4 no longer names both feather takers, since each of its triggers (8466 Grazle, 8467 Nafien) shows only one. Converted: the opening is the 8460 and 8461 premises; parts: 1 Grazle's thanks and the road to Nafien (QUEST_DONE 8460, QUEST_ACCEPT 8462), 2 Nafien's welcome and warning (QUEST_DONE 8462), 3 the Felpaw camp broken (QUEST_DONE 8461), 4 the feathers (QUEST_DONE 8466, 8467, auto-complete repeatables), 5 the Deadwood totem (QUEST_DONE 8470). Dropped 'Beyond lies Winterspring, where the Winterfall have fallen to the same corruption': that is Salfa's 8465 reward, left to Winterspring with 8464, 8465 and 8469. npc_text 8123 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: village direction made southwest (see Deadwood Village). Faction 0 confirmed: 8460 and 8461 races 0, Grazle and Nafien template 35. Entry points: 8460 (Grazle) and 8461 (Nafien, no prerequisite). Salfa's Winterfall quests (8464, 8469) and 8465 are left to Winterspring. 6131/6221/6241 are old duplicates and unused.

parts.body: Grazle takes the help as a sign of growing friendship, for the Timbermaw suffer much from the events of the past, and he sends the proven north along the road to Nafien. The guard may look a feral and unsavory beast, Grazle warns, but he is not to be feared: he only seeks aid against the malign forces that threaten their home.

Nafien has heard word on the wind of outsiders seeking the Timbermaw's friendship, and he welcomes them, but warns that his tribe reacts poorly to strangers. In these trying times they trust only those who fight the corruption alongside them and prove it, and any who have not will be met with open hostility within the Hold.

When the camp is broken, Nafien senses the victory without needing to hear of it. Victory, he says, is a hollow word for what had to be done. Still, the deed proves its doer worthy, and though it may take time before the Timbermaw welcome them without hostility, perseverance will wear down suspicion, so long as no weapon is ever raised against the tribe.

Trust grows slowly. The suspicious brethren of the tribe still need convincing, and the distinctive headdresses some Deadwood wear give proof of every blow struck against them: each set of feathers brought in makes the bearer's deeds known among the Timbermaw.

Inside the Hold, Kernda takes a Deadwood ritual totem thick with the stench of decay. Whatever foulness has turned the Deadwood against their kin, Kernda says, is surely present in it, and through study and ritual the Timbermaw hope to uncover what pollutes the minds of their brethren.
